key_insight: Detonation-spraying parameters can tune the roughness, thickness, and hydrophobicity of titanium-dioxide-based metal–ceramic coatings.
engineering_relevance: The reported relationships can guide nozzle-speed and spray-distance selection to target coating geometry and maximize hydrophobicity.
method: Vary detonation-spraying conditions for titanium-dioxide-based coatings.
Assess surface roughness, coating thickness, and contact angle.
Derive parameter–property equations and identify conditions for maximum hydrophobicity.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports inverse-power relationships between nozzle travel speed and both roughness and thickness, plus parabolic relationships linking spray distance to roughness and contact angle.
watch_item: The abstract provides no numerical optimum, tested parameter ranges, or prediction errors, limiting direct transfer to production.
paper_title: Surface Characteristics of Titanium Based Coatings Obtained by Detonation Spraying Under Various Process Conditions
